Morgan Carter  
Member ID: W450765041  
Harvard Pilgrim Health Care—Commercial/ACA, Maine  
Reference number: POC-99CC30886D-55239  
Requested service: Lumbar fusion  
CPT: 22612  

[Date]

Harvard Pilgrim Health Care  
Appeals and Grievances Department

Re: Appeal of denial of prior authorization for lumbar fusion

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I appeal Harvard Pilgrim’s denial dated August 7, 2026. The denial states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity. I request that Harvard Pilgrim reopen and approve the prior authorization for the requested lumbar fusion, CPT 22612, based on the enclosed clinical documentation.

The publicly available guideline identified for this request is the 2026 Evolent Clinical Guidelines for Medical Necessity Review—Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines, Evolent Clinical Guideline 1766 for Lumbar Spine Surgery, effective July 1, 2026. The guideline includes CPT 22612 among the codes for single-level lumbar fusion.

The policy states:

“Operative treatment is indicated only when the natural history of surgically treated lesions is better than the natural history for non-operatively treated lesions.”

“All operative interventions must be based on a positive correlation with clinical findings, the natural history of the disease, the clinical course, and diagnostic tests or imaging results.”

“All individuals being considered for surgical intervention should receive a comprehensive neuromusculoskeletal examination to identify pain generators that may either respond to non-surgical techniques or may be refractory to surgical intervention.”

“All appropriate supporting documentation, including recent pertinent office visit notes, laboratory data, and results of any special testing must be provided.”

“In order for surgeries to be considered medically necessary there must be clear medical records that demonstrate a clear surgical plan that matches the request for surgery.”

The submitted records address these requirements as follows:

1. Clinical findings and progressive course  
I have had 12 months of progressive lower-back and leg pain that has not been relieved by rest. I have neurogenic claudication, diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes, and leg pain and heaviness that force me to stop after standing or walking for more than 10 minutes. Sitting provides relief.

2. Imaging and correlation with the clinical findings  
The June 23, 2026 lumbar MRI and flexion-extension radiographs demonstrate grade I degenerative spondylolisthesis at L4-L5, 5 mm of translation on flexion-extension, and severe central stenosis compressing the cauda equina. These findings correspond to the clinical picture of neurogenic claudication and bilateral L5 sensory loss.

3. Failure of conservative treatment  
The physical therapy discharge note documents 24 supervised visits over 10 weeks, from April 15, 2026, through June 24, 2026, including core stabilization and lumbar-flexibility treatment. Despite completing this course, symptoms remain progressive and functionally limiting. I also used NSAIDs for six months with inadequate relief. A corticosteroid injection on April 10, 2026, produced only two weeks of partial relief.

4. Examination and relevant medical information  
The records document the neuromusculoskeletal examination findings, including neurogenic claudication and diminished sensation in both L5 dermatomes. The records also document no bowel or bladder dysfunction. There is no active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, and no smoking history.

5. Surgical plan  
The requested service is lumbar fusion, CPT 22612, for the documented L4-L5 degenerative spondylolisthesis and severe central stenosis. The treating surgeon is Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery. Please review the surgeon’s submitted operative plan and confirm that it matches the requested CPT code and the L4-L5 pathology shown on the imaging.

These records provide the clinical history, failed conservative treatment, examination findings, imaging, functional limitations, and surgical information needed to evaluate medical necessity. If Harvard Pilgrim still considers the submission incomplete, please identify each specific missing record or data element and provide the exact clinical-review criteria applied to this request. Please do not issue another general incomplete-documentation denial without identifying what information is missing.

Please overturn the denial and approve the requested lumbar fusion. If approval is not granted, please provide the complete clinical rationale, the specific criteria applied, the records considered, the records found insufficient, and instructions for the next level of appeal or external review.

This appeal must be received by February 3, 2027, which is 180 days after the August 7, 2026 denial notice.

Sincerely,

Morgan Carter

Enclosures:

- August 7, 2026 adverse benefit determination  
- Physical therapy discharge note documenting 24 visits from April 15, 2026, through June 24, 2026  
- June 23, 2026 lumbar MRI report  
- June 23, 2026 flexion-extension radiograph report  
- Medication and treatment history  
- April 10, 2026 corticosteroid-injection record  
- Orthopedic surgical consultation and operative plan from Okafor, MD  
- Relevant examination and clinical notes
